sections.h2: Can I search Clay County property records online?
sections.html:
Not at this time, according to the clerk. The Clay County Clerk's page says deed records are digitized back to the 1960s and that property records are currently not available online. Plan to call or visit the clerk's office in Henrietta, and ask for the record by owner name, legal description or instrument number.

The clerk's page adds two limits owners should know. The clerk cannot give legal advice or services, and the clerk has no duty to search public records, citing Attorney General opinion WW-607. A title company or attorney does the searching.

sections.h2: Where is the Clay County Clerk's office and when is it open?
sections.html:
The office is in the Courthouse Annex at 214 N. Main Street, Henrietta, TX 76365, with a mailing address of P.O. Box 548. The phone is (940) 538-4631 and the fax is (940) 264-4160. Hours are Monday to Friday, 7:30 a.m. to 4:00 p.m., and the annex closes from noon to 1:00 p.m. every day.

  • The office closes for major holidays.
  • It may close for court hearings, training or bad weather, so call before a long drive.
  • Historic Commissioners' Court record books from the 1870s have been restored and are kept in the clerk's office.

sections.h2: What ID do I need to file a deed in Clay County?
sections.html:
A government photo ID. A notice posted by the clerk explains that Senate Bill 16, effective September 1, 2025, adds Local Government Code 191.010(b): the clerk must require photo ID from whoever presents a document for the real property records, must copy it, and must reject the filing if the person refuses.

The notice describes the law as a statewide deed fraud measure. It also tightens criminal penalties for real property theft and fraud, lets victims seek restitution and a no-fee judicial voiding of a fraudulent deed, and sets stronger standards for notaries. A seller who plans to mail a deed should ask the clerk how the ID rule applies to documents delivered by a title company.

sections.h2: What does the Clay County Clerk charge to record a deed?
sections.html:
The first page costs $25 in total, and each added page costs $4, based on the clerk's fee schedule effective September 1, 2025. Other recording lines from that schedule are below.

Clay County Clerk recording fees as printed in the schedule effective September 1, 2025
FilingFirst page, totalEach added page
Official Public Records (deeds, releases)$25.00$4.00
State tax lien or release$15.00$4.00
Federal tax lien or release$30.00$4.00
Plat inside city limits$85.00not listed
Plat outside city limits$325.00not listed

The $25 first-page figure is built from a $10 archive fee, a $5 recording fee and a $10 records management fee. Each name to be indexed beyond five adds $0.25.

sections.h2: What mistakes make the Clay County Clerk charge extra or refuse a deed?
sections.html:
Format errors raise the price or stop the filing, and the schedule lists them:

  • No grantee mailing address on a deed signed after December 31, 1981 brings a penalty equal to the greater of twice the filing fee or $25, on top of regular fees.
  • No clear heading at the top of the first page doubles the filing fee for that page.
  • Names not legibly typed or printed under each signature double the fee for that page.
  • Printed type must be no smaller than 8 point, per the schedule's citation of Local Government Code 191.007.
  • The deed needs original signatures and a proper acknowledgment under Property Code 12.001(b).

Copies cost $1.00 per page, certification is $5.00 per document, and a notice of trustee sale carries a $2.00 fee. A returned check costs $30.

sections.h2: Which state recording rules sit behind Clay County's fee schedule?
sections.html: The Texas county clerk manual describes the clerk as the county recorder, with deed records filed in the county where the land lies. It lists the instruments a clerk records, among them general and special warranty deeds, quitclaim deeds, trustee's deeds, sheriff's deeds, tax deeds, deed of trust releases and powers of attorney. The manual also lets a commissioners court tell the clerk to waive real property recording fees for buyers using certain federal or state grant programs. Ask the Henrietta office whether that option has been adopted.

sections.h2: How do probate and heirs affect a Clay County house sale?
sections.html:
If an owner has died, a probate filing may be needed before the house can be sold. The County Clerk's fee schedule lists a base probate or guardianship filing at $360, and $418 when a citation is issued and posted by the sheriff. A will left for safekeeping with the clerk costs $16. The clerk's page also links a guardianship registration form and civil court cost instructions.

Ask the clerk or a Texas attorney which route fits a particular estate. County clerks cannot advise on that choice, as the clerk's page states plainly.

sections.h2: What does the Clay Appraisal District handle?
sections.html:
Value and exemptions, but not tax collection. The Clay County Appraisal District FAQ says it does not levy taxes, set rates or collect them, and that you must call the proper tax office for amounts. Its site, claycad.org, carries forms, an interactive map, protest hearing information and an oil and gas FAQ.

  • Homestead exemption: you must have owned and lived in the home on January 1, and it must be your principal residence. The district says the claim covers up to 20 acres of residential land.
  • Filing window: January 1 to April 30 of the tax year, with a late homestead claim allowed up to two years after taxes become delinquent.
  • Over 65: the claim can be filed up to one year after the 65th birthday, with proof of age.
  • Mobile homes can be set up as improvement-only accounts if you file a request for separate taxation with the title or a verified purchase contract.

The Comptroller calendar gives May 15, or the 30th day after notice is delivered when later, as the usual protest deadline. The CAD FAQ adds that a protest letter need not be on an official form.

sections.h2: What do the Census figures say about Clay County?
sections.html:
Clay is a thinly settled county. Census QuickFacts reports a July 2025 estimate of 10,764 people, up from 10,218 at the 2020 census, on 1,088.76 square miles. That works out to 9.4 people per square mile in 2020.

  • Housing units: 5,247, with only 8 building permits in 2025
  • Owner-occupied rate: 84.0%, across 4,289 households
  • Median owner-occupied home value: $171,500 for 2020 to 2024
  • Median gross rent: $811; median household income: $80,114
  • Residents 65 or older: 24.7%

With so few sales, a comparable house may be miles away. Ask a title company for recent recorded deed prices in your part of the county.

faqs.q: Are Clay County property records available online?
faqs.a: No. The Clay County Clerk's page says deed records are digitized back to the 1960s but that property records are currently not available online. Call (940) 538-4631 or visit the annex in Henrietta.

faqs.q: What are the hours of the Clay County Clerk?
faqs.a: Monday to Friday, 7:30 a.m. to 4:00 p.m., with the annex closed from noon to 1:00 p.m. daily. The office may close for hearings, training or bad weather.

faqs.q: Do I need a photo ID to record a deed in Clay County?
faqs.a: Yes. Under Local Government Code 191.010(b), added by Senate Bill 16 effective September 1, 2025, the clerk must require photo ID from the person presenting a real property document, copy it and reject the filing if the person refuses.

faqs.q: How much does it cost to record a deed in Clay County?
faqs.a: The clerk's schedule effective September 1, 2025 lists $25 for the first page and $4 for each added page. Missing grantee addresses, a missing heading or unreadable printed names add penalties.

faqs.q: Who collects property tax in Clay County?
faqs.a: Not the appraisal district. The Clay CAD says it does not collect taxes, so call the proper tax office for amounts. The appraisal district's site lists a separate Pay Taxes Online link for that purpose.
